# Database

PostgreSQL 16. 106 tables across 26 migrations, grouped by area rather than by
change, so the schema can be read as a description of the product.

SQLite is not supported, even for tests. The schema relies on `jsonb`, partial
unique indexes, check constraints and `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; a suite passing
on a different engine would not have exercised the guarantees the product
depends on.

## Conventions

**Keys.** ULID primary keys (`char(26)`), generated by the application.

**Tenancy.** Every tenant-owned table carries `organization_id` with a foreign
key to `organizations`, and it is the leading column of the indexes that matter.
See [security.md](security.md) for how it is enforced.

**Money.** Integer minor units (`bigint`) plus a `currency` column beside it.
There is no `decimal` amount anywhere. A row that can be reported in the
organization's own currency also carries `base_*` columns and the
`exchange_rate` used, because the rate that applied on the day is part of the
record.

**Time.** `timestamptz` for instants, `date` for calendar facts. A stay night is
a date; a capture is an instant.

**Structured data.** `jsonb`, used for genuinely shapeless things — a webhook
payload as it was sent, a cancellation policy snapshot, provider metadata. Never
as a way to avoid a column that queries need.

**Deletion.** Records that participate in money or in history are not deleted.
Properties, listings and channel accounts are archived or disconnected;
reservations are cancelled; ledger entries are reversed. Soft deletes exist on
a few directory tables where a genuine mistake needs undoing.

## The tables, by area

### Tenancy, identity and access

```
organizations           the tenant
users                   a person; may belong to several organizations
memberships             a person's seat in one organization
membership_role         which roles that seat holds
membership_permission   per-seat grants and revocations on top of the roles
membership_property     property restriction, when a seat is limited
roles                   system roles (organization_id null) and tenant copies
permissions             107 rows, synced from the registry by permissions:sync
permission_role
invitations             a pending seat; invitation_role carries its roles
login_histories         every attempt, successful or not
audit_logs              who changed what, with before and after values
sessions                Laravel's session table
personal_access_tokens  Sanctum's tokens
```

A role is a system role when `organization_id` is null. An organization
customising one gets its own copy; the original is never edited, so a later
change to the registry cannot silently widen somebody's access.

### Portfolio

```
portfolios              a grouping an operator defines
complexes               a building or development holding several properties
properties              the sellable asset
property_rooms          rooms within a property
property_photos         files on a private disk; only the key is stored
units                   individual keys in a multi-unit property
unit_types              the sellable class ("one-bed garden view")
amenities               the shared catalogue, synced by amenities:sync
amenity_property
amenity_listing
listings                what is offered for sale, and where
listing_photos          an explicit selection, overriding the property's
listing_versions        every published change, append-only
```

A property is the asset; a listing is an offer. They are separate because one
apartment can be sold as a whole, as two rooms, or under two brands, and each of
those is a different offer with different content, rates and restrictions.

### Reservations and availability

```
reservations               the booking
reservation_nights         one row per night, carrying that night's rate
reservation_charges        accommodation, fees, taxes, discounts, upsells
reservation_guests         who is actually staying
reservation_status_changes every transition, with who and why
calendar_days              per-listing overrides: rate, minimum stay, closures
calendar_blocks            owner stays, maintenance, manual holds
quotes                     a priced, frozen offer with an expiry
```

`reservation_nights` is the load-bearing table in the whole product. Revenue is
attributed night by night, which is what lets a stay spanning a month boundary,
a rate change or a change of ownership split correctly. Anything that attributes
a booking wholly to its check-in date is wrong in a way nobody notices until an
owner queries a statement.

### Pricing and tax

```
rate_plans          independent or derived from a parent
pricing_rules       seasonal, day-of-week, length-of-stay, last-minute, orphan
fee_rules           cleaning, extra guest, pet, resort — each with its basis
tax_rules           percentage or per-person-per-night, with caps and exemptions
promotions          codes and automatic discounts
cancellation_policies  the refund schedule; snapshotted onto each reservation
```

The policy is snapshotted onto the reservation at booking. Changing your
cancellation terms next year must not retroactively change what a guest who
booked this year is owed.

### Guests and owners

```
guests                first-class, deduplicated, with lifetime statistics
owners                individuals and companies
property_ownerships   dated shares; both ends nullable meaning open-ended
management_agreements the commission terms, dated, per owner and property
tags, taggables       shared tagging
custom_fields, custom_field_values
```

Ownership is dated because properties change hands mid-year. A statement
attributes each night using the shares in force *on that night*.

### Operations

```
tasks                  cleaning, maintenance, inspection, restocking, requests
task_checklist_items   with per-item photo requirements
task_photos
task_comments
task_recurrences       templates that generate work on a schedule
checklist_templates    per organization, optionally per property
teams, team_members
staff_availability, staff_time_off
vendors                external contractors
```

Tasks generated by the turnover scheduler carry a `generation_key`, unique per
reservation and purpose, which is what makes regeneration idempotent when a
booking moves.

### Messaging

```
conversations       one thread per booking party
messages            inbound, outbound and internal notes in one thread
message_templates   with a documented variable vocabulary
saved_replies
notifications, notification_preferences
automation_rules, automation_runs
```

Internal notes live in the same thread as guest messages. The context of "guest
asked for a late checkout" and "the cleaner can't do it before one" is the same
context, and separating them loses it.

### Money

```
payments                 with is_simulated and is_collected_by_us
refunds
payment_schedules        deposit now, balance later
expenses                 with markup, and who it is billed to
ledger_accounts          the chart of accounts, installed per organization
journal_entries          posted entries are immutable
journal_lines            debit and credit, in transaction and base currency
owner_statements         frozen on approval
owner_statement_lines    signed so the column adds up to the closing balance
owner_payouts            with a masked destination snapshot
document_sequences       per-organization, per-kind human references
```

Corrections are made by reversal, never by editing a posted entry. A payout
records the destination *as it stood when the money moved*, masked, because a
payout that went to an account the owner has since changed went to the old one.

### Distribution

```
channel_accounts    a connection; credentials encrypted and hidden on the model
channel_listings    the mapping, with dirty flags per dimension
sync_jobs           every conversation with a channel, including is_simulated
```

`availability_dirty` and `rates_dirty` are separate flags because they are
pushed separately and fail separately. They are the answer to "why is this still
bookable there?".

### Guest experience

```
reviews             with the source's own rating scale kept alongside a percent
upsell_products, upsell_orders
documents           per guest, reservation, property or owner
smart_locks         with is_simulated
access_codes        with a CHECK that valid_until > valid_from
```

### Platform and integrations

```
domain_events       the event store; the integration seam
api_keys            only a SHA-256 hash is stored
webhook_endpoints   signing secret encrypted, never returned
webhook_deliveries  what was sent, byte for byte, with the response
saved_reports       parameters and a delivery schedule
idempotency_keys
```

`webhook_deliveries` carries a partial unique index:

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX webhook_deliveries_attempt_unique
ON webhook_deliveries (webhook_endpoint_id, domain_event_id, attempt)
WHERE domain_event_id IS NOT NULL;
```

Partial, because a test delivery has no originating event and several of those
are legitimate. For real events it makes a redelivered job harmless.

### Simulated providers

```
simulated_payment_transactions
simulated_locks, simulated_access_codes
simulated_message_deliveries
```

These are the state of the local stand-in implementations — not fixtures. The
mock lock really tracks battery level and code slots; the mock payment provider
really holds authorisations. Their separateness is the point: nothing in the
real tables is fabricated, and a query against `payments` never picks up a row
that exists only to make a screen look busy.

## Polymorphic relations

Every morph type is registered in `config/morph-map.php` and
`Relation::enforceMorphMap()` is on. A model that is not registered throws when
`getMorphClass()` is called, which turns "somebody renamed a class and three
years of audit rows now point at nothing" into a failing test.

## Migrations

Grouped by area, and each one has a working `down()`. CI migrates from an empty
database, seeds the demo through the real services, and rolls the whole thing
back — because a migration that only ever runs against a database somebody else
already migrated is a migration nobody has tested.
